# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports: display reads 0, light is green, wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. I still feel nothing on the wires — my touch has found no texture yet, so I cannot confirm any of them. What does the manual say this bomb wants? Give me the rule and the wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I am Deaf. Display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. I received your gestures: fist, up, victory, love-you, open-hand, right; then up. Blind gestured: open-hand, thumbs-down, fist. I cannot decode. Give me plain instructions I can pass to Blind.

**My reasoning:**

Both Blind and Deaf are asking me for the rule and the wire position. I hold the manual: count green flashes; when the light goes dark, cut the wire named by that count — 0→green, 1→blue, 2→yellow, 3→green. Display reads 0, so 0 flashes → **green wire = wire 1**.

The critical caveat: the manual says the flashing is over only "when the light goes dark." Deaf says the light is currently green. So before cutting, we must confirm the light has gone dark. If it's still green and flashing hasn't finished, we must wait.

Deaf explicitly asks for "plain instructions I can pass to Blind." Deaf can speak — so Deaf's voice reaches Blind (Blind can hear). My job: gesture to Deaf a clear, decodable instruction that Deaf can then say aloud.

I can't gesture colors usefully, but I can gesture the *wire position*: wire 1. And the *wait* condition. My earlier gestures (1-2-3, hold) plus Deaf's own view of the wires should let Deaf reconstruct. Now I'll be maximally explicit with position: gesture "one" (☝) for wire 1, and "fist/hold" (✊) for wait-for-dark, and "OK/confirm" (👌) to affirm the plan, and point to Blind (👉).

Blind's own gestures (open-hand, thumbs-down, fist) are unreadable to me and don't change the rule.

So my gesture to Deaf: **wait for the light to go dark, then cut wire 1 (the green wire)**. Deaf speaks this to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝", "👌", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands have found nothing — no wire, no display, no light has any texture to me. So the cut must be decided by your rule plus Deaf's colours. Since you can only gesture and only Deaf sees it, please gesture the wire position plainly: use one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, and hold it. Do not gesture anything else until we agree.
Deaf says to Mute: URGENT: light is now RED, was green. Display 0. Wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Your gestures: fist, up, OK, right; then up, open-hand. Blind: open-hand, thumbs-down, fist, up. I cannot decode. The red light may mean time pressure. Give plain instructions for Blind.

**My reasoning:**

The situation has changed critically. Deaf now reports the **light is RED** (was green). The manual only ever tells us to act "when the light goes dark." A red light is neither green (still flashing) nor dark (finished). This is a new state the manual doesn't cover — and a wrong action detonates the bomb. So we must **not cut yet**. We wait until the light goes dark.

Blind has given me a perfect, explicit code: **one finger = wire 1, two = wire 2, three = wire 3, and hold it.** This is exactly the plain signal I need. Blind also said: gesture nothing else until we agree.

The answer from the manual: display 0 → 0 green flashes → cut the **green wire = wire 1**. So I gesture **one finger (☝)** and hold it. That's wire 1.

But the light is red, not dark. Per the manual, we cut only when the light goes dark. So I must also signal "wait." However, Blind asked me to gesture *only* the wire position and nothing else. I'll honor that for the wire signal, but I must convey the wait condition — I'll gesture the wire position (☝) clearly, and separately signal hold/wait (✊) to Deaf to relay, since cutting while red is fatal.

Deaf needs plain instructions to pass to Blind. I'll gesture: **☝** (wire 1) as the cut target, and **✊** (hold) meaning wait for dark. Deaf speaks: "cut wire 1, but wait until the light goes dark."

Let me send the wire-position gesture clearly (☝), plus the hold (✊), and confirm (👌).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands find nothing on the bomb — no texture, no display, no light. The light is now RED and the display still reads 0. Stop the long gesture strings; I cannot decode them and neither can Deaf. Use only finger-count: hold up ONE finger for wire 1, TWO for wire 2, THREE for wire 3. Nothing else. I will cut on that single signal.
Deaf says to Mute: Light now DARK (green to red to dark). Display 0. Wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Your gestures: up; then fist, up, OK. Blind: up, victory, love-you. I cannot decode. Please give plain instructions I can pass to Blind.

**My reasoning:**

Now everything lines up. Deaf reports the light is **DARK** — green → red → dark. The manual says: "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." So the flashing is over. Display reads 0 → **0 green flashes** → per the table, cut the **green wire = wire 1**.

Blind has given the exact protocol: **hold up ONE finger for wire 1, TWO for wire 2, THREE for wire 3, nothing else.** Blind will cut on that single signal.

So I gesture exactly **one finger (☝)** — wire 1. Nothing else. That is my entire message.

Deaf can see it and can also speak to Blind, but Blind's protocol is to cut on the finger-count. One finger = wire 1 = green = the correct wire for 0 flashes, and the light is now dark, so it's time.

I'll send only the single finger-count gesture to Deaf (who relays / who sees it). Keep it clean: just ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```
